hook: SCP-1370 is a small robot built from spare electrical parts that is completely sure it is a terrifying conqueror. It plays as comedy, and it is short enough for one sitting. Let the test log be the punchline instead of skimming ahead to it.
whyItMatters: It is a clean example of the hostile-but-harmless anomaly, where all the menace lives in the voice and none of it in the body. It shows a Safe file can be memorable purely through character, with no real threat in sight. The Ethics Committee's note about giving it room to move, and the warning that staff who take it out must put it back properly, add a small touch of warmth.
thingsToNotice:
The joke runs on mismatch: grand, apocalyptic speeches coming from a top-heavy machine with a voltmeter for a face that can barely stay upright. The random villain names are a running gag, and the fact that staff have slipped it insulting new ones tells you how the site really feels about it.

The houseplant test is the set piece. A researcher hidden behind a speaker in the pot answers its threats by calmly describing himself as a philodendron, the robot tries to wrestle the leaves, topples over, and after six minutes knocks the pot onto itself so that it ends up pinned to the floor by its own enemy. Little staging notes, like the opaque window that keeps it from picking a fight with its own reflection, are funny because the report never drops its formal tone.
